title: Protective effect of pH-sensitive carvacrol zinc oxide quantum dots on Nrf-2, MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways and protein-bound carbohydrates in DMBA-induced mammary carcinogenesis.
authors: Srinivasan, Manoj Kumar; Aruchamy, Mohanprasanth; Namasivayam, Nalini; Muthupandian, Saravanan
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦pH敏感香芹酚-ZnO量子点对DMBA诱导乳腺癌中Nrf-2/MAPK/NF-kB通路及蛋白结合碳水化合物的保护作用，核心为小分子-蛋白互作与癌症治疗，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common malignancy among women worldwide, with increasing incidence and significant mortality rates. Conventional treatment strategies, including chemotherapy and radiation, often lead to adverse side effects and may not effectively prevent cancer recurrence or metastasis. pH-sensitive nanoparticles offer a promising alternative, leveraging the acidic tumor microenvironment for targeted drug delivery with minimal systemic toxicity. This study investigates the therapeutic potential of pH-sensitive carvacrol-ZnO quantum dots (CVC-ZnO QDs) in a DMBA-induced mammary cancer model in female Sprague-Dawley rats. The study specifically examines the impact of CVC-ZnO QDs on protein-bound carbohydrate levels and the molecular regulation of Nrf-2, MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways. Four experimental groups were analyzed: a control group, a DMBA-induced cancer group, a CVC-ZnO QDs-alone treated group and a combined DMBA and CVC-ZnO QDs-treated group. Results revealed that DMBA-induced mammary cancer led to significant elevations in protein-bound carbohydrates, including hexose, hexosamine and sialic acid. CVC-ZnO QDs administration effectively restored these levels to near-normal concentrations. Immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR and Western blot analyses demonstrated that CVC-ZnO QDs significantly downregulated MAPK and NF-kappaB expression while upregulating Nrf-2, suggesting enhanced antioxidant defense and suppression of tumor-promoting pathways. Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinities of CVC to Nrf-2, MAPK and NF-kappaB, with key hydrogen bonding interactions contributing to the stability of ligand-protein complexes. These findings highlight the potential of CVC-ZnO QDs as a novel therapeutic strategy for breast cancer, offering targeted cytotoxicity with reduced systemic toxicity. Further studies are warranted to explore the clinical translatability of these nanocarriers in breast cancer treatment.
abstract_zh: 乳腺癌是全球女性中最常见的恶性肿瘤，其发病率不断上升且死亡率显著。传统治疗策略，包括化疗和放疗，常导致不良副作用，且可能无法有效预防癌症复发或转移。pH敏感纳米颗粒提供了一种有前景的替代方案，利用酸性肿瘤微环境实现靶向药物递送，并具有最小全身毒性。本研究探讨了pH敏感香芹酚-ZnO量子点（CVC-ZnO QDs）在雌性Sprague-Dawley大鼠DMBA诱导的乳腺癌症模型中的治疗潜力。研究特别考察了CVC-ZnO QDs对蛋白结合碳水化合物水平以及Nrf-2、MAPK和NF-kappaB通路分子调控的影响。分析了四个实验组：对照组、DMBA诱导癌症组、CVC-ZnO QDs单独处理组以及DMBA和CVC-ZnO QDs联合处理组。结果显示，DMBA诱导的乳腺癌症导致蛋白结合碳水化合物显著升高，包括己糖、己糖胺和唾液酸。CVC-ZnO QDs给药有效将这些水平恢复至接近正常浓度。免疫组织化学、qRT-PCR和Western blot分析表明，CVC-ZnO QDs显著下调MAPK和NF-kappaB表达，同时上调Nrf-2，提示增强了抗氧化防御并抑制了肿瘤促进通路。分子对接确认了CVC与Nrf-2、MAPK和NF-kappaB的强结合亲和力，关键氢键相互作用有助于配体-蛋白质复合物的稳定性。这些发现突显了CVC-ZnO QDs作为乳腺癌新型治疗策略的潜力，提供靶向细胞毒性并减少全身毒性。需要进一步研究以探索这些纳米载体在乳腺癌治疗中的临床转化可行性。
